deviations: cs_bucket_rank (the design's own worked example for `leaf_slots`, both in the '2. Generator' section and the WP5 step list) does not exist in AlphaCube's registry -- it is a Partura-plugin-only ND kernel. tests/test_daily_leaf_typing.py (WP2) hit the identical gap and documented the same fix: substitute `cs_regres`, the only other ND-face, arity-2, non-boolean, non-resource-risk operator AlphaCube ships. Used in test_leaf_slots_fills_only_the_named_slot.

JUDGMENT CALL on op_weight's accepted shape, since the design text is internally ambiguous here (not a source-vs-design conflict, since this is new code): the '2. Generator' code stub types op_weight strictly as Callable[[OpSpec], float], but the WP5 construction-time-validation prose says 'every op_weight key names a registered operator; every value is a finite float >= 0' and the test list says 'an unknown operator name ... each raise at __init__' and 'a weight table that empties the pool' -- vocabulary (key/value/table) that only makes sense for a Mapping, and a pure callable gives __init__ no way to ever see an 'unknown name' (it is only ever called with real OpSpec objects already pulled from the registry). Resolution shipped: op_weight accepts EITHER a callable(OpSpec)->float (called directly, exactly as the design's pseudocode shows) OR a {operator name: weight} Mapping (validated against the registry and wrapped into such a callable by the new _resolve_op_weight; an unlisted name defaults to the uniform weight 1.0). self.op_weight is always, after __init__, the callable form -- so _pick_weighted's code is unaffected and matches the design's pseudocode verbatim. Flagging this because WP7's SearchHooks (not yet built) forwards its own op_weight straight into this parameter: either shape works.

Found and had to work around a real tension inside the design's own WP5 text, not a mistake on my part: a literally-all-zero op_weight (e.g. `lambda s: 0.0`) is simultaneously (a) the worked example for 'all-zero weights still return an operator via the uniform fallback' in the generator test-plan bullet, and (b) exactly what 'a weight table that empties the 26-spec reduce pool' means in the construction-time-validation bullet -- and (b) is required to raise ValueError at __init__. These cannot both be true of the SAME op_weight value. Resolution: construction-time validation raises for a GLOBALLY all-zero (or pool-emptying) op_weight, as the design's own IndexError/ShapeError-forever justification demands. The 'all-zero weights still return an operator' property is real and tested, but as a property of `_pick_weighted` itself for an arbitrary draw whose specs happen to be all zero-weighted (e.g. a single mutate_operator call's narrow per-node `alts`, which __init__ cannot enumerate ahead of time) -- tested in test_op_weight_all_zero_for_one_draw_still_returns_an_operator and test_op_weight_uniformly_zero_draw_matches_the_plain_uniform_path by reassigning gen.op_weight AFTER construction (bypassing the one-time __init__ check) and calling _pick/_pick_weighted directly.
result.notes:
New public names on TypedTreeGenerator, for WP7's SearchHooks and Partura's ac_plugin to build on: constructor keywords op_weight, accept, daily_fields, daily_leaf_prob, leaf_slots, on_exhausted ('fallback'|'raise'), mutation_checks_bans (bool); new attributes self.op_weight (always a callable(OpSpec)->float after __init__, or None), self.accept_hook, self.hook_rng (a second random.Random, seeded (seed*2654435761)&0xFFFFFFFF -- any accept hook MUST draw from gen.hook_rng, never gen._rng, or the steer/control comparison stops being reproducible from the seed), self.unaccepted_fallbacks (int counter); public method acceptable() unchanged in signature but now also consults the hook; new private _ban_ok/_pick_weighted/_resolve_op_weight/_check_weight/_check_accept_hook helpers (not exported); module now exports GenerationExhausted(ValueError) via __all__, plus the module-level GENERATE_FALLBACK_TRIES=64 constant (importable but not added to __all__, matching the design's instruction to export only GenerationExhausted). acceptable()'s order is is_valid_root -> _ban_ok -> accept_hook, matching the design exactly, including the short-circuit that keeps one_layer_keys() uncomputed when there is no ban set.

Backward compatibility was the thing I verified hardest, two independent ways: (1) an RNG-call-sequence recorder (random.Random subclass logging every method name) run through the new _pick versus a hand-frozen copy of the literal pre-WP5 _pick body, confirming identical call sequences AND identical picks, not just equal keys; (2) [e.key() for e in generate_population(40)] identical between a plain generator and one constructed with every new keyword passed explicitly at its documented default. Both pass. The two "deliberate behaviour changes" the design calls out (mutate_window/mutate_constant now checking the ban+hook; generate()'s fallback now checking them too) are pinned with the design's own two concrete leak examples (cross_quantile_q25(day_argmax(Low), 3) under O:day_argmax(F:Low) banned; mul(day_cov(Volume, Low), 2.0) under O:day_cov(F:Volume,F:Low) banned), each shown to leak under mutation_checks_bans=False and to be sealed under the new default.

Low-confidence spot for a reviewer to double check: the exact wording of the ValueError messages (op_weight emptying the pool; negative/NaN weight; unknown operator name; bad accept) -- the design says only "Raise ValueError naming the cause", not exact strings, so I chose the phrasing myself (visible in generator.py's _check_weight/_check_accept_hook/_resolve_op_weight/__init__). If WP7's tests or Partura's own error-matching code string-match on exact phrasing, they will need to match what I actually shipped. Also: op_weight's construction-time value check evaluates the hook over self.specs (the generator's own vocabulary, ~214 by default) rather than registry.list_all() (244) -- deliberate, since those are exactly the specs _pick/_pick_weighted ever see, but worth knowing if a future caller expects validation against the full registry instead.

Did not touch mining/gp.py, plugins.py, scoring.py, or anything outside the two owned files -- GPMiner's own hooks=/SearchHooks plumbing is WP7's job per the design's dependency graph (WP5 depends only on WP2, which was already committed in this worktree). Verified via git status/git diff --stat that only the two owned files changed, and the full suite was run against this worktree's own src/ (via the repo-root conftest.py's sys.path insert, confirmed by reading it directly), not any globally installed alphacube.
